statement: In electronics and signal processing, noise is an unwanted random disturbance in an electrical signal, typically modeled as an additive perturbation to a useful information signal: $y = s + n$, where $s$ is the information signal, $n$ is the noise disturbance characterized by stochastic properties such as its variance, probability distribution, and spectral density $N_0(f)$, and $y$ is the observed signal.

symbols.meaning: noise power spectral density at frequency f

properties.property: A noise signal is typically modeled as a linear addition to a useful information signal.
properties.why: noise energy superposes onto the channel or circuit containing the information signal

properties.property: Uncorrelated noise sources add according to the sum of their powers.
properties.why: powers of uncorrelated stochastic signals sum directly without cross-interference terms

properties.property: Thermal noise is approximately white with a constant power spectral density across frequency and an amplitude with nearly a Gaussian probability density function.
properties.why: it is generated by the random thermal motion of charge carriers inside an electrical conductor regardless of applied voltage

properties.property: Root-mean-square shot noise current satisfies the Schottky formula $i_n = \sqrt{2 I q \Delta B}$.
properties.why: charge carriers traversing a steep potential barrier exhibit independent, discrete arrival times

properties.property: Flicker noise ($1/f$ noise) has a pink power spectral density that falls off steadily into higher frequencies.
properties.why: it arises from device-level conductance fluctuations and semiconductor defects

properties.property: Noise voltage density is expressed in volts per root hertz ($\mathrm{V}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$).
properties.why: power in a resistive element is proportional to the square of voltage, so voltage density equals the square root of power spectral density

properties.property: Partition noise occurs when current divides among two or more paths, producing noise exceeding combined shot noise.
properties.why: random fluctuations occur during the division of charge carriers between paths

assumptions.assumption: Noise sources are uncorrelated, allowing noise powers to be summed directly.
assumptions.breaks_when: Noise sources are correlated with each other or with the signal (e.g., quantization error).

assumptions.assumption: Thermal noise behaves as additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN).
assumptions.breaks_when: System operates near absolute zero where quantum noise dominates, or non-white noise processes dominate the frequency spectrum.

assumptions.assumption: Shot noise follows the Schottky formula assuming independent discrete arrivals across a potential barrier.
assumptions.breaks_when: Space charge is present to smooth arrival times, electrons move diffusively in bulk conductors without a barrier, or current splits among multiple paths.

assumptions.assumption: Noise combines linearly with the signal.
assumptions.breaks_when: Signals share a non-linear medium, producing intermodulation noise.

failure_modes.signature: Noise input impedance of a transistor drops and noise rapidly increases with frequency, dominating all other noise sources.
failure_modes.cause: The time required for charge carriers to travel across the device becomes comparable to the period of the amplified signal (VHF and above).

failure_modes.signature: Sudden step-like transitions between two or more discrete voltage or current levels up to several hundred microvolts lasting milliseconds to seconds.
failure_modes.cause: Random and unpredictable switching processes occurring at semiconductor defects.

failure_modes.signature: Unwanted noise voltage hum or interference across circuit ground connections.
failure_modes.cause: Voltage differences existing between separate ground connection points instead of a common equipotential ground bus.

failure_modes.signature: Measured RMS current noise is significantly less than predicted by the Schottky formula.
failure_modes.cause: Accumulation of space charge smooths out carrier arrival times, decreasing current randomness.
